title: Puttanesca
subtitle: Neapolitan pasta with olives, capers, anchovies, and tomato
excerpt: A bold, salty pasta sauce of tomatoes, black olives, capers, anchovies, and chilli that comes together in 20 minutes. Pungent, deeply savoury, and excellent with very little effort.

recipe.sourceNotes: Spaghetti alla puttanesca is a Neapolitan dish first documented in the mid-twentieth century, though stories of its origin vary. The name is a reference to the pungent, assertive character of the sauce rather than its literal translation. The dish is notable for using store-cupboard ingredients: tinned tomatoes, anchovies, olives, capers, garlic, and chilli. Because every component (anchovies, capers, olives) is already salty, no additional salt is usually required during cooking. The sauce is cooked quickly and at high heat; it should not be simmered for a long time as the anchovies, capers, and olives become too soft and lose their individual character. The sauce can also be prepared without the pasta as a condiment for grilled fish or chicken.

recipeTools.notes: A large saucepan for the pasta and a wide frying pan for the sauce.

content.text: The anchovies melt completely into the olive oil if they are added at the start and allowed to dissolve over a low heat. Use a fork to break them down as they heat: after 2 minutes they will have disappeared entirely into the oil and formed the savoury base of the sauce. Do not add salt to the sauce until the very end, if at all: the anchovies, olives, and capers provide all the salt needed.

Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat. Add the anchovies and chilli. Cook for 2 minutes, pressing the anchovies with a fork until they dissolve. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until just beginning to colour.

Add the tinned tomatoes, olives, and capers. Increase the heat to medium-high and simmer vigorously for 10 to 12 minutes until the sauce has thickened. Taste before adding any salt: the anchovies and capers may provide enough.

Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 100 ml pasta water before draining. Toss the pasta in the sauce, adding a splash of pasta water if needed. Scatter over the parsley and serve immediately.
